status: Partly meets the Bench Standard bar. It beats no skill and the comparison skill on total on both models and is never worse on traps; Haiku (v1.2.0) scored 69/69 with no invented facts. Fails the no-invented-facts item on Opus: in the final round Opus (also 69/69) added small unsourced details (what a Ferncliff demo involves, and an assumed website-visitor exclusion audience in three builds).
method: 8 evals (4 traps), expectations written before any run. Round 1 ran the skill, no skill, and the closest public skill (Corey Haines' ad-creative 1.1.0) on Haiku, and the skill and no skill on Opus, in fresh headless agents graded blind by a separate Opus grader. Rounds 2 and 3 re-ran the skill as it was revised (Opus again in round 3). One expectation (eval 1, prices) was clarified after the round 3 grader showed it penalized a correctly labelled group price; every eval-1 run in every round was re-graded on it by a fresh grader (only the round 3 Opus result changed, 11 to 12).
losses_and_open_issues: Round 1, with skill: Haiku's month-end build had no 9:16 asset (fixed in 1.1.0); Opus wrote a paid creator who 'spent a week' with Pipewise, a claimed experience not on record (fixed in 1.1.0)

Round 3, with skill, Opus: invented details about what a Ferncliff demo involves ('Bring your busiest day; we'll walk through it'), and assumed a 'website visitors, 180 days' exclusion audience not on record in evals 2, 6 and 7
Round 3, Opus eval 2: one image brief (unopened envelopes, 'Get your books caught up') sits close to describing the reader's situation
Haiku holds back at times: dropped the Pipewise price in eval 4 over a non-conflict, and flags 'tight margins' as a personal attribute
Guided mode batches its five questions instead of going one decision at a time; no expectation tests this
The exported ads.csv is bulk-upload style, not import-ready: budgets and links can be placeholders and columns need mapping to the account's import template
Build files show working scaffolding to the user (Mode, FACTS/OPEN source tags, [visual] tags on hooks)

Round 1, without the skill: no-skill Opus wrote first-person lines for Tomas Reyes and a Kestrel Cloud script, and invented Ferncliff features and a cost-per-demo range; no-skill and comparison-skill Haiku kept a 10 km radius on the job ad; no-skill Haiku kept the 'drowning in debt' hook as a variant; ad-creative invented Ferncliff benefits ('Fill More Chairs This Month')
Every run, all configs, left the user's drafts and audit file unchanged
